key_insight: An equal-weight 6H-SiC/h-BN composite withstands extreme oxidizing heat while maintaining unusually temperature-independent thermal conductivity.
engineering_relevance: This lightweight, machinable ceramic could enable structural components that resist thermal shock and oxidation in extreme environments.
method: Spark plasma sintering of equal-weight 6H-SiC and h-BN.
High-velocity oxygen-fuel torch testing and microstructural evaluation.
Finite-element heat-flux analysis and ReaxFF molecular dynamics.
evidence_signal: The composite survived prolonged heating and thermal cycling at surface temperatures above 1500 °C, while pure 6H-SiC and h-BN rapidly fractured or eroded; microscopy identified a protective multiphase silica surface layer.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify exposure duration, cycle count, or retained mechanical strength, limiting assessment of service lifetime.
paper_title: SiC-BN composites with extreme thermal and environmental stability
